title: Subscription credential unavailable messages must use centralized sandbox constants
answers: Where is the Claude subscription credential unavailable message defined?
How to raise ProcessTaskFatalError when model credentials fail to arrive in a task sandbox?
Why do sandbox tests assert against CLAUDE_CREDENTIAL_UNAVAILABLE_MESSAGE?
body:
Subscription credential failure messages must be defined as shared constants in products/tasks/backend/logic/services/sandbox.py:CLAUDE_CREDENTIAL_UNAVAILABLE_MESSAGE and products/tasks/backend/logic/services/sandbox.py:CODEX_CREDENTIAL_UNAVAILABLE_MESSAGE rather than duplicated string literals.
Launcher preflight in products/tasks/backend/logic/services/agent_server_launcher.py:_agent_server_preflight, credential error handling in products/tasks/backend/logic/services/agent_server_launcher.py:_credential_unavailable_error, and health checks in products/tasks/backend/logic/services/sandbox.py:wait_for_health_check must reference these constants when raising ProcessTaskFatalError.
Sandbox test suites in products/tasks/backend/logic/services/tests/test_docker_sandbox.py and products/tasks/backend/logic/services/tests/test_modal_sandbox.py must assert against the shared constants.
This prevents wording drift between runtime error handling, tests, and API or Desktop credential relay instructions.
applies: Tasks backend sandbox services and agent launcher error handling
says: Coding agent sandbox crashes without explanation when AI subscription keys are missing
Provide clear error when model subscription credentials are unavailable in the workspace
Standardize error message displayed when automated agent encounters missing subscription credentials
Cloud task fails abruptly if AI provider credentials cannot be delivered
